title: Lawn quoting, recurring schedules and seasonal calendar
audience: Lawn and turf business owners, office staff and crew leaders who quote, schedule and sell recurring lawn care.
learningOutcomes: Build a lawn quote that separates recurring mowing from seasonal services and one-off work.
Design a recurring schedule that matches the lawn's growth, the site's access and the client's expectations.
Use a seasonal calendar that sets out when each service is appropriate and when it should be deferred.
Explain the scope, exclusions and variation rules to the client in writing.

instruction.heading: How recurring lawn work creates volume
instruction.body: Recurring lawn work is the base of many lawn businesses because it creates predictable volume. A client who signs up for a fortnightly mow, or a weekly mow in peak season, gives the business regular income and a steady route. Volume grows when the business adds seasonal services such as edging, aeration, dethatching and topdressing, and when it sells them to the same client in the right season. The key is to design the offer so that each service fits the lawn's needs at that time of year. A calendar that sells the wrong service at the wrong time damages trust and leads to disputes. Build the offer from what the lawn needs, not from what is easiest to sell.

instruction.heading: Quoting the recurring service
instruction.body: Quote the recurring mowing separately from the seasonal services. The recurring quote should state the frequency, the mowing height, the edging included, the waste removal, the access, the site area and the exclusions. Price the recurring visit for the time, the equipment, the travel, the waste and the risk controls, not for the area alone. Adjust for difficult sites such as slopes, many obstacles, long travel or restricted access, and record the reason for the adjustment. Exclusions should be listed in writing, including product application unless the business is authorised for it at that location, tree work, irrigation repairs and any work at height. Use the business's pricing method, shown in {{business:pricing.pricing_method}}, and get written approval through {{business:pricing.quoting_approval}} before the schedule starts.

instruction.heading: Building the seasonal calendar
instruction.body: A seasonal calendar sets out the services that suit each part of the year for the species and the region. Use the species identified on the job record, and use the local climate and the client's site conditions. In general, the calendar should show when mowing frequency rises and falls, when edging is done, when aeration or dethatching is appropriate, when fertiliser is considered, and when weed control is considered under the product rules. Mark the periods when services should be deferred, such as drought, flood recovery or dormancy. The calendar is a planning tool and is not a guarantee.

instruction.heading: Writing the schedule and the variation rules
instruction.body: Write the schedule with the dates or the frequency, the services included, the services that require separate approval, and the conditions under which a visit may be moved or cancelled. Include the weather rule: when rain or extreme heat makes a visit unsafe or damaging, the business may reschedule, and the client is told in advance where possible. Set out the variation rule in writing. A change to the schedule, the area or the service is a variation that needs approval before the work starts and a price change recorded. A recurring client who asks for an extra service mid-season should receive a written variation, not a verbal add-on. Review the schedule with the client at least once a season, and record the review.

instruction.heading: Client communication and records
instruction.body: Explain the offer in plain language at the first meeting, and check that the client understands what is included, what is seasonal, what is excluded and what needs approval. Use the same terms in the quote, the calendar and the schedule so that the client does not receive three different descriptions. Keep a record of every conversation that changes the scope, including the date, who was present and what was agreed. Store the calendar and schedule in the client file, and give the client a copy. A clear, consistent record protects the business if a dispute arises about what was promised, and it helps the crew arrive prepared for each visit.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the quote, the schedule and the calendar against the job record. A competent office or crew leader can show how the recurring quote was built, explain the exclusions, describe the seasonal calendar and identify what must be approved before work starts. Escalate any quote where the scope is unclear, any request for product application without confirmed authority, any schedule that conflicts with the lawn's condition, and any client who disputes a variation.

procedure: Confirm the species, site area, access, slopes and obstacles from the site visit and the job record.
Quote the recurring mowing separately, stating the frequency, mowing height, edging, waste and exclusions.
Add any seasonal services as separate quoted items, each with its timing and its deferral conditions.
Build the seasonal calendar for the species and region, marking the periods when services should be deferred.
Write the schedule with the weather rule, the rescheduling rule and the variation rule.
Obtain the client's written approval before the first visit.
Review the schedule and calendar at least once a season, and record the review and any variation.
File the quote, the approval, the calendar and the review in the client record.

workedExamples.situation: A client with a sloping lawn and a long driveway asks for a fortnightly mow and asks whether edging and aeration can be included at the same price.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you quote the recurring service and the seasonal services?
workedExamples.reasoning: Quote the fortnightly mow with the slope, the access and the waste included in the recurring price. Quote edging as part of the recurring visit if the scope says so, and quote aeration separately as a seasonal service with its own timing and deferral conditions. Record the exclusions, get written approval, and do not promise the aeration result or fold it into the flat mowing price.

workedExamples.situation: In the middle of a dry period a recurring client asks for aeration to be done on the next visit.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you agree, and what do you put in writing?
workedExamples.reasoning: Refer to the seasonal calendar, which marks aeration as deferred during drought stress. Explain the reason to the client and offer a date when the calendar allows it. Record the request and the decision, and issue a written variation if the client wants to proceed later.

equipmentAndPpe: Recurring quote template with scope, exclusions and frequency
Site visit record with species, area and access notes
Photographs of the lawn taken with consent for the record

commonErrors.error: Folding seasonal services into the flat recurring price without recording them.
commonErrors.prevention: Quote seasonal services separately, with timing, deferral conditions and approval.

commonErrors.error: Selling aeration or dethatching in the wrong season.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the calendar and the lawn's condition before offering any seasonal service.

commonErrors.error: Agreeing to an extra service by phone and doing it on the next visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Issue a written variation and get written approval before the work starts.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result, such as a green lawn by a set date.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe what the service does and what conditions affect its result, and record the limits in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Quotes and schedules must not include product application or tree work unless the business is authorised for that work at that location. Product authority is covered in the lawn product lesson.
Check the business's terms before issuing them.

qualityStandard: Every recurring quote lists frequency, mowing height, edging, waste, access, exclusions and approval status.
Seasonal services are quoted separately, with timing and deferral conditions shown on the calendar.
Every variation is in writing and approved before work starts.
The schedule is reviewed and the review is recorded at least once each season.
documentationEvidence: Signed recurring quote with scope and exclusions.
Seasonal calendar provided to the client, with the species and region noted.
Variation records with dates and approvals.
Seasonal review record for each client.
summary: Recurring mowing is the base of the offer. Seasonal services are quoted separately and sold in the right season.
Price the recurring visit for time, equipment, travel, waste and risk, and record the exclusions.
Use a calendar that marks deferral periods, and do not sell services that the lawn does not need.
Put every variation in writing and get approval before the work starts.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a recurring mowing quote be built?
options: By the lawn area only, with everything else included without listing it on the quote
By the frequency, mowing height, edging, waste and access, with exclusions listed in writing.
By a flat rate that the crew agrees on the day, based on the size of the lawn and the crew

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for aeration during a drought period. What does the seasonal calendar suggest?
options: Proceed immediately, because clients always want the service done as soon as possible
Add it to the recurring visit without a note, since the client already paid for it
Defer aeration until the lawn has recovered, explain the reason and offer a date.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for an extra service mid-season over the phone. What is the correct handling?
options: Issue a written variation, get approval and record the price change before the work starts.
Do it on the next visit and add it to the invoice later, since the client will agree to the change
Refuse the request without explanation, since the schedule is already full for the season
